jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

jobs.title: Data & Analytics Leader/Architect
jobs.description:
Data & Analytics Leader/Architect

Full Time

Toronto, ON (Hybrid)

The opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Data & Analytics Leader to help shape and grow enterprise transformation programs across the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance sector. This role brings together data strategy, analytics, AI, consulting, business development, executive advisory, and delivery leadership. You will work with senior client stakeholders to define transformation priorities, shape large-scale opportunities, and guide teams from strategy through measurable value realization.

What you will do

• Build trusted relationships with CDOs, CIOs, CAIOs, business executives, and senior technology leaders.
• Advise BFSI clients on enterprise data strategy, analytics transformation, AI adoption, governance, modernization, and operating models.
• Translate complex business challenges into practical transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and measurable outcomes.
• Lead executive workshops, discovery sessions, steering committee discussions, and strategic client conversations.
• Drive growth for Data, Analytics, and AI services from opportunity identification and qualification through proposal, negotiation, and closure.
• Shape large consulting and transformation engagements, including solution direction, value proposition, commercial approach, and delivery roadmap.
• Lead RFPs and proactive proposals, ensuring solutions are differentiated, feasible, and focused on business outcomes.
• Build joint opportunities with account teams, alliance partners, technology providers, and consulting practices.
• Define target-state strategies across cloud data platforms, data products, analytics, AI/ML, GenAI, governance, and responsible AI.
• Provide executive oversight from opportunity shaping and mobilization through delivery, governance, and value realization.
• Lead and mentor consulting, architecture, engineering, analytics, and AI teams across locations.
• Develop reusable offerings, reference architectures, case studies, estimators, executive narratives, and delivery playbooks.

What you bring

• 18+ years of experience across data, analytics, AI, consulting, and enterprise transformation, including leadership of large-scale programs.
• Deep expertise in enterprise data strategy, data architecture, governance, operating models, data products, and data modernization.
• Strong understanding of data engineering, including ETL/ELT
, integration, APIs, orchestration, data quality, observability, DataOps
, and platform engineering.
• Experience leading analytics and BI initiatives, including enterprise reporting, self-service analytics, semantic layers, advanced analytics, and decision intelligence.
• Knowledge of AI, machine learning, Generative AI, Agentic AI, MLOps/LLMOps, responsible AI, and AI-led business transformation.

• Experience defining enterprise solutions across Azure, AWS, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake
, and other modern data platforms.
• Strong knowledge of BFSI requirements, including regulatory compliance, privacy, security, resilience, auditability, and risk management.

• Proven success in consulting, business development, presales, solutioning, opportunity qualification, proposals, pricing support, and executive stakeholder management.
• Ability to lead global, cross-functional teams and engage effectively with CXOs and senior business leaders.
• Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline. A master's degree, MBA, and relevant cloud, architecture, data, analytics, AI, or program certifications are preferred.

jobs.title: Director, Sponsor Analytics
jobs.description:
The Director, Sponsor Analytics will lead the Sponsor Analytics function within Group Benefits, with primary accountability for delivering meaningful, actionable insights and reporting to plan sponsors, Distribution partners and internal business leaders.

The Director will shape the strategy and evolution of sponsor reporting and analytics, ensuring sponsors have access to trusted, relevant and increasingly sophisticated insights to better understand their benefits programs, member populations and key areas of opportunity. Through improved use of data and insights, the role will support informed decisions that contribute to healthier outcomes and the health and well-being of Canadians.

The Director will also lead and contribute to broader analytics initiatives across Group Benefits where the team’s capabilities, data and expertise can create value, including strategic business priorities, portfolio analytics, operational insights, customer and member analytics, and emerging analytical needs.

Working closely with Plan Sponsor Services, Distribution, Product, Operations, Data and Technology partners, the Director will lead the development and evolution of standardized and customized reporting, self-service analytics, data products and insights. The role will balance evolving sponsor and business needs with scalable solutions, strong data governance, appropriate data protection and a focus on business value and customer outcomes.

The Director will lead and develop a high-performing analytics team, establishing clear priorities, strengthening analytical capabilities and fostering a culture focused on meaningful outcomes for sponsors and the broader Group Benefits business.

Position Responsibilities

Lead the Sponsor Analytics function and team. Establish priorities and a roadmap aligned with the Group Benefits sponsor reporting and analytics strategy, while coaching and developing a collaborative, accountable and high-performing team.
Partner with plan sponsors, Distribution and business leaders. Translate sponsor and business needs into meaningful reporting, analytics and insights, balancing individual requests with strategic priorities and scalable solutions.
Advance the sponsor reporting strategy. Evolve traditional reporting toward proactive, insight-driven analytics that help sponsors understand their benefits programs, emerging trends and opportunities for action.
Lead sponsor-facing analytics products and reporting. Oversee standardized and customized reporting, dashboards and self-service capabilities, ensuring a consistent and effective sponsor experience.
Use analytics to improve outcomes for sponsors and members. Identify trends, opportunities and insights that support informed benefits decisions and contribute to improving the health and well-being of Canadians.
Support broader Group Benefits analytics priorities. Apply the team’s capabilities and expertise to strategic business questions across product, customer, member, portfolio and operational analytics.
Identify emerging analytical opportunities. Partner with business leaders to frame questions, assess available data, develop analytical approaches and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Strengthen data storytelling. Translate complex information into clear, relevant and actionable insights for sponsors, Distribution partners and senior business leaders.
Drive consistency, efficiency and automation. Simplify reporting and analytical processes, reduce manual effort and create reusable capabilities that scale across Group Benefits.
Advance the analytics data ecosystem. Partner with Data and Technology teams to establish the data, platforms and capabilities required for reliable, timely and increasingly sophisticated analytics.
Champion data quality, governance and protection. Ensure reporting and analytical products use trusted data and adhere to enterprise governance, privacy and data protection standards.
Establish measures of success. Define and monitor adoption, stakeholder value, reporting effectiveness, operational efficiency and advancement of analytical capabilities.
Drive innovation and continuous improvement. Assess emerging technologies, analytical techniques and business opportunities that can improve sponsor insights and create value across Group Benefits.
Represent Sponsor Analytics in cross-functional forums. Ensure sponsor reporting and broader analytics requirements are considered in Group Benefits data, product and technology decisions.

Required Qualifications

University degree in business, finance, analytics, technology, mathematics, engineering or another quantitative field. An advanced degree is considered an asset.
Significant leadership experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting or a related data function, including leading teams through change and transformation.
Strong experience developing client-, sponsor- or externally facing analytics and reporting solutions and translating complex data into meaningful business insights.
Demonstrated ability to apply analytics across business problems, including recurring reporting, exploratory analysis, strategic insights and scalable analytical solutions.
Strong understanding of the Group Benefits business and the needs of plan sponsors, Distribution partners and internal stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing analytics and reporting strategies that balance immediate stakeholder needs with longer-term scalable capabilities.
Experience partnering with Distribution and client-facing teams and using data visualization and storytelling to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience with modern analytics, business intelligence and data technologies, including dashboards, automated reporting and self-service analytics.
Ability to identify analytical opportunities, structure ambiguous business questions and translate data into recommendations and business outcomes.
Strong understanding of data quality, governance, privacy and protection, particularly for sponsor- or external-facing reporting.
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into analytical solutions, challenge requests appropriately and prioritize based on sponsor and business value, strategic alignment and organizational capacity.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to establish credibility with senior leaders, Distribution partners and cross-functional teams.
Ability to work effectively in a complex, matrixed organization and align business, data and technology partners around shared objectives.
Curious, pragmatic and outcome-oriented, with a passion for using data and analytics to improve the sponsor experience, support healthier outcomes and drive better business decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Root Financial is a US based financial consulting firm that provides fractional, high-impact finance and accounting leadership to growing businesses. We are seeking a Director of Finance and Accounting
to serve as an embedded, on-site consultant for our client in Toronto, ON.

This position requires a blend of strategic FP&A (budgeting, forecasting, cash modeling) and core operational accounting (month-end close, financial reporting, clean books). Operating as a senior individual contributor, you will be embedded directly within our client’s leadership team to drive financial visibility, streamline accounting processes, and support strategic growth.

POSITION DETAILS

Location:
Toronto, ON (Greater Toronto Area)
Work Arrangement:
100% Full-Time On-Site (at Fulfillment IQ’s Toronto office)
Employment Type:
Full-Time Employee (Root Financial)
Compensation:
CAD $140,000–$165,000 base, plus a 10% target bonus

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Accounting and close
Own monthly, quarterly and year-end close across US, Canadian and Indian entities in QuickBooks Online
Manage intercompany accounting, transfer pricing support and multi-currency consolidation (CAD, USD, INR)
Keep revenue recognition (ASC 606) accurate across services and software revenue
Run AP/AR, payroll accounting, accruals, prepaids and bank reconciliations, and lead FIQ's India-based accounting team
Build and document controls and workflows across QBO, Ramp, Expensify, Docket and HubSpot

FP&A and reporting
Maintain the group financial model, rolling cash forecasts and annual budgets by entity
Deliver monthly budget-vs-actual reporting and KPIs: project margin, utilization, ARR for software products
Prepare board materials and lender reporting, including covenant compliance
Manage cash and treasury across banking relationships

Tax, compliance and strategic support
Coordinate with external tax advisors on US and Canadian filings, GST/HST and SR&ED claims
Support the legal entity reorganization, IP transfer, equity plan administration and 409A work
Support audits, fundraising due diligence and new entity setup

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Experience:
8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, with required background in the Professional Services
or agency industry.
Technical Expertise:
Advanced, hands-on proficiency with QuickBooks Online (QBO)
and advanced Excel financial modeling skills.
Accounting Standards:
Solid foundation in accrual accounting, GAAP principles, and financial reporting.
Role Fit:
Proven track record as a self-directed individual contributor with strong client-facing communication skills and high attention to detail.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

jobs.title: Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
University Hospital Foundation

The University Hospital Foundation is dedicated to a powerful, singular purpose: to continuously seek, inspire and support bold solutions to seemingly insurmountable challenges and ignite new discoveries in health. Responsible for raising and managing funds to advance innovation in prevention, research and patient care, the Foundation strives to transform and redefine health in the Edmonton area, throughout Alberta and around the world so everyone can live a longer, healthier life.

In the past ten years, generous donations from individuals and our corporate and strategic partners have contributed nearly $220 million to advance world-leading patient care at the University of Alberta Hospital, Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute, and Kaye Edmonton Clinic, as well as groundbreaking research at the University of Alberta.

As an outcome-focused organization, UHF offers a flexible hybrid working environment. To learn more about the University Hospital Foundation, visit www.GiveToUHF.ca and if you have a keen interest in being a part of the future of healthcare in Alberta, please consider applying today!

The Opportunity

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and reporting to the President & CEO, the Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer. plays a critical role in developing and implementing the business and financial strategy and enabling systems strategy of the University Hospital Foundation (the Foundation). This position is integral to organizational success in support of the mission, vision, values, and goals of the Foundation.

This role serves as a critical advisor to the President & CEO, the Executive Leadership team and support to the Board of Trustees including their supporting committees.

This role leads the Finance, People & Technology Portfolio and manages a diverse department of professionals who are passionate about contributing to the Foundation’s mission through providing the most efficient and effective operational support. This role is a pivotal member of the leadership team that embraces change as an opportunity to learn and is constantly looking for ways to improve the level of service to internal and external customers.

Key accountabilities include financial and operational activities in the areas of finance & investments, accountability of funded projects, donation services, fund management and distributions, information technology & management, people practices, legal & risk management, and facilities & property management.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Provide strategic management and oversight to the People, Finance and Technology teams to align with UHF’s long-term strategy to support multiple stakeholders including donors and funding recipients.
Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, compliance, investment oversight, and stewardship of donor funds.
Support the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board committees with clear, timely, and strategic advice.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by modernizing systems, strengthening operational capacity, and encouraging new ways of working.
Advance the Foundation’s technology strategy and roadmap, using technology to improve processes, productivity, decision-making, and organizational scalability.
Ensure strong governance, risk management, legal, privacy, procurement, and compliance practices.
Build and lead a collaborative, customer-centric team that provides excellent service to internal and external stakeholders.
Foster trusted relationships with donors, partners, board members, auditors, investment managers, government representatives, and health-system stakeholders.
Contribute to a culture that is accountable, courageous, innovative, collaborative, and focused on measurable impact.

Qualifications and Experience

The ideal candidate is an innovative, experienced executive financial and operational leader with the ability to translate strategy into effective systems, structures, and results.

They will bring a strong track record in financial stewardship, people leadership, technology-enabled transformation, risk management, and organizational capacity building. Experience in a complex not-for-profit, charitable, healthcare, post-secondary, public-sector, or similarly mission-driven environment would be considered an asset.

Education & Experience

Preferred qualifications include:

A professional accounting designation, such as CPA, or equivalent senior financial leadership experience.
A post-secondary degree in business, finance, human resources, or a related discipline; an MBA or relevant graduate degree would be an asset.
Significant senior financial leadership experience, including experience in a CFO or comparable executive role.
Proven experience leading teams through growth, change, transformation, or modernization.
Strong knowledge of financial planning, investment oversight, fund accounting, reporting, compliance, and risk management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors or Board of Trustees and supporting board-level committees.
Demonstrated expertise in leveraging data, systems, and technology to drive organizational performance, inform strategic decision-making, and advance enterprise priorities.

Behavioral Competencies and Personal Attributes

The Successful Candidate Will Be

Strategic, financially astute, and future-focused.
Innovative and curious, with a willingness to challenge the status quo and explore better ways to deliver impact.
Collaborative, approachable, and able to build trust across teams, partners, and stakeholders.
A clear communicator who can make complex financial and operational matters understandable to non-financial audiences.
Customer-centric, service-oriented, and committed to supporting both internal teams and external partners.
Courageous, accountable, and comfortable leading through ambiguity and change.
A values-driven leader who operates with integrity, sound judgment, and humility.

Measurements of Success Within the First Year

Success In The First Year Will Include

Building trusted relationships with the Board of Trustees, President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, direct reports, and key external stakeholders.
Establishing clear priorities, accountabilities, and decision-making practices across the enabling systems portfolio
Strengthening finance, people, technology, and operational systems to support improved service, efficiency, and scalability.
Advancing a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and exceptional customer experience.
Supporting strategic partnerships across the health, life sciences, wellness, philanthropic, and public-sector ecosystems.
Contributing meaningfully to organizational priorities, including leadership development, inclusion, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability.

If you are interested in this role and meet the above criteria, please click the “Apply”
button to send your resume directly to Sumbul Hameed or Jay Borchert.

Partner with plan sponsors, Distribution and business leaders. Translate sponsor and business needs into meaningful reporting, analytics and insights, balancing individual requests with strategic priorities and scalable solutions.
Advance the sponsor reporting strategy. Evolve traditional reporting toward proactive, insight-driven analytics that help sponsors understand their benefits programs, emerging trends and opportunities for action.
Lead sponsor-facing analytics products and reporting. Oversee standardized and customized reporting, dashboards and self-service capabilities, ensuring a consistent and effective sponsor experience.
Use analytics to improve outcomes for sponsors and members. Identify trends, opportunities and insights that support informed benefits decisions and contribute to improving the health and well-being of Canadians.
Support broader Group Benefits analytics priorities. Apply the team’s capabilities and expertise to strategic business questions across product, customer, member, portfolio and operational analytics.
Identify emerging analytical opportunities. Partner with business leaders to frame questions, assess available data, develop analytical approaches and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Strengthen data storytelling. Translate complex information into clear, relevant and actionable insights for sponsors, Distribution partners and senior business leaders.
Drive consistency, efficiency and automation. Simplify reporting and analytical processes, reduce manual effort and create reusable capabilities that scale across Group Benefits.
Advance the analytics data ecosystem. Partner with Data and Technology teams to establish the data, platforms and capabilities required for reliable, timely and increasingly sophisticated analytics.
Champion data quality, governance and protection. Ensure reporting and analytical products use trusted data and adhere to enterprise governance, privacy and data protection standards.
Establish measures of success. Define and monitor adoption, stakeholder value, reporting effectiveness, operational efficiency and advancement of analytical capabilities.
Drive innovation and continuous improvement. Assess emerging technologies, analytical techniques and business opportunities that can improve sponsor insights and create value across Group Benefits.
Represent Sponsor Analytics in cross-functional forums. Ensure sponsor reporting and broader analytics requirements are considered in Group Benefits data, product and technology decisions.

Required Qualifications

University degree in business, finance, analytics, technology, mathematics, engineering or another quantitative field. An advanced degree is considered an asset.
Significant leadership experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting or a related data function, including leading teams through change and transformation.
Strong experience developing client-, sponsor- or externally facing analytics and reporting solutions and translating complex data into meaningful business insights.
Demonstrated ability to apply analytics across business problems, including recurring reporting, exploratory analysis, strategic insights and scalable analytical solutions.
Strong understanding of the Group Benefits business and the needs of plan sponsors, Distribution partners and internal stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing analytics and reporting strategies that balance immediate stakeholder needs with longer-term scalable capabilities.
Experience partnering with Distribution and client-facing teams and using data visualization and storytelling to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience with modern analytics, business intelligence and data technologies, including dashboards, automated reporting and self-service analytics.
Ability to identify analytical opportunities, structure ambiguous business questions and translate data into recommendations and business outcomes.
Strong understanding of data quality, governance, privacy and protection, particularly for sponsor- or external-facing reporting.
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into analytical solutions, challenge requests appropriately and prioritize based on sponsor and business value, strategic alignment and organizational capacity.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to establish credibility with senior leaders, Distribution partners and cross-functional teams.
Ability to work effectively in a complex, matrixed organization and align business, data and technology partners around shared objectives.
Curious, pragmatic and outcome-oriented, with a passion for using data and analytics to improve the sponsor experience, support healthier outcomes and drive better business decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

new_jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Root Financial is a US based financial consulting firm that provides fractional, high-impact finance and accounting leadership to growing businesses. We are seeking a Director of Finance and Accounting
to serve as an embedded, on-site consultant for our client in Toronto, ON.

This position requires a blend of strategic FP&A (budgeting, forecasting, cash modeling) and core operational accounting (month-end close, financial reporting, clean books). Operating as a senior individual contributor, you will be embedded directly within our client’s leadership team to drive financial visibility, streamline accounting processes, and support strategic growth.

POSITION DETAILS

Location:
Toronto, ON (Greater Toronto Area)
Work Arrangement:
100% Full-Time On-Site (at Fulfillment IQ’s Toronto office)
Employment Type:
Full-Time Employee (Root Financial)
Compensation:
CAD $140,000–$165,000 base, plus a 10% target bonus

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Accounting and close
Own monthly, quarterly and year-end close across US, Canadian and Indian entities in QuickBooks Online
Manage intercompany accounting, transfer pricing support and multi-currency consolidation (CAD, USD, INR)
Keep revenue recognition (ASC 606) accurate across services and software revenue
Run AP/AR, payroll accounting, accruals, prepaids and bank reconciliations, and lead FIQ's India-based accounting team
Build and document controls and workflows across QBO, Ramp, Expensify, Docket and HubSpot

FP&A and reporting
Maintain the group financial model, rolling cash forecasts and annual budgets by entity
Deliver monthly budget-vs-actual reporting and KPIs: project margin, utilization, ARR for software products
Prepare board materials and lender reporting, including covenant compliance
Manage cash and treasury across banking relationships

Tax, compliance and strategic support
Coordinate with external tax advisors on US and Canadian filings, GST/HST and SR&ED claims
Support the legal entity reorganization, IP transfer, equity plan administration and 409A work
Support audits, fundraising due diligence and new entity setup

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Experience:
8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, with required background in the Professional Services
or agency industry.
Technical Expertise:
Advanced, hands-on proficiency with QuickBooks Online (QBO)
and advanced Excel financial modeling skills.
Accounting Standards:
Solid foundation in accrual accounting, GAAP principles, and financial reporting.
Role Fit:
Proven track record as a self-directed individual contributor with strong client-facing communication skills and high attention to detail.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

new_jobs.title: Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
University Hospital Foundation

The University Hospital Foundation is dedicated to a powerful, singular purpose: to continuously seek, inspire and support bold solutions to seemingly insurmountable challenges and ignite new discoveries in health. Responsible for raising and managing funds to advance innovation in prevention, research and patient care, the Foundation strives to transform and redefine health in the Edmonton area, throughout Alberta and around the world so everyone can live a longer, healthier life.

In the past ten years, generous donations from individuals and our corporate and strategic partners have contributed nearly $220 million to advance world-leading patient care at the University of Alberta Hospital, Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute, and Kaye Edmonton Clinic, as well as groundbreaking research at the University of Alberta.

As an outcome-focused organization, UHF offers a flexible hybrid working environment. To learn more about the University Hospital Foundation, visit www.GiveToUHF.ca and if you have a keen interest in being a part of the future of healthcare in Alberta, please consider applying today!

The Opportunity

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and reporting to the President & CEO, the Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer. plays a critical role in developing and implementing the business and financial strategy and enabling systems strategy of the University Hospital Foundation (the Foundation). This position is integral to organizational success in support of the mission, vision, values, and goals of the Foundation.

This role serves as a critical advisor to the President & CEO, the Executive Leadership team and support to the Board of Trustees including their supporting committees.

This role leads the Finance, People & Technology Portfolio and manages a diverse department of professionals who are passionate about contributing to the Foundation’s mission through providing the most efficient and effective operational support. This role is a pivotal member of the leadership team that embraces change as an opportunity to learn and is constantly looking for ways to improve the level of service to internal and external customers.

Key accountabilities include financial and operational activities in the areas of finance & investments, accountability of funded projects, donation services, fund management and distributions, information technology & management, people practices, legal & risk management, and facilities & property management.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Provide strategic management and oversight to the People, Finance and Technology teams to align with UHF’s long-term strategy to support multiple stakeholders including donors and funding recipients.
Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, compliance, investment oversight, and stewardship of donor funds.
Support the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board committees with clear, timely, and strategic advice.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by modernizing systems, strengthening operational capacity, and encouraging new ways of working.
Advance the Foundation’s technology strategy and roadmap, using technology to improve processes, productivity, decision-making, and organizational scalability.
Ensure strong governance, risk management, legal, privacy, procurement, and compliance practices.
Build and lead a collaborative, customer-centric team that provides excellent service to internal and external stakeholders.
Foster trusted relationships with donors, partners, board members, auditors, investment managers, government representatives, and health-system stakeholders.
Contribute to a culture that is accountable, courageous, innovative, collaborative, and focused on measurable impact.

Qualifications and Experience

The ideal candidate is an innovative, experienced executive financial and operational leader with the ability to translate strategy into effective systems, structures, and results.

They will bring a strong track record in financial stewardship, people leadership, technology-enabled transformation, risk management, and organizational capacity building. Experience in a complex not-for-profit, charitable, healthcare, post-secondary, public-sector, or similarly mission-driven environment would be considered an asset.

Education & Experience

Preferred qualifications include:

A professional accounting designation, such as CPA, or equivalent senior financial leadership experience.
A post-secondary degree in business, finance, human resources, or a related discipline; an MBA or relevant graduate degree would be an asset.
Significant senior financial leadership experience, including experience in a CFO or comparable executive role.
Proven experience leading teams through growth, change, transformation, or modernization.
Strong knowledge of financial planning, investment oversight, fund accounting, reporting, compliance, and risk management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors or Board of Trustees and supporting board-level committees.
Demonstrated expertise in leveraging data, systems, and technology to drive organizational performance, inform strategic decision-making, and advance enterprise priorities.

Behavioral Competencies and Personal Attributes

The Successful Candidate Will Be

Strategic, financially astute, and future-focused.
Innovative and curious, with a willingness to challenge the status quo and explore better ways to deliver impact.
Collaborative, approachable, and able to build trust across teams, partners, and stakeholders.
A clear communicator who can make complex financial and operational matters understandable to non-financial audiences.
Customer-centric, service-oriented, and committed to supporting both internal teams and external partners.
Courageous, accountable, and comfortable leading through ambiguity and change.
A values-driven leader who operates with integrity, sound judgment, and humility.

Measurements of Success Within the First Year

Success In The First Year Will Include

Building trusted relationships with the Board of Trustees, President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, direct reports, and key external stakeholders.
Establishing clear priorities, accountabilities, and decision-making practices across the enabling systems portfolio
Strengthening finance, people, technology, and operational systems to support improved service, efficiency, and scalability.
Advancing a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and exceptional customer experience.
Supporting strategic partnerships across the health, life sciences, wellness, philanthropic, and public-sector ecosystems.
Contributing meaningfully to organizational priorities, including leadership development, inclusion, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability.

If you are interested in this role and meet the above criteria, please click the “Apply”
button to send your resume directly to Sumbul Hameed or Jay Borchert.
